summary:
EarthScope AI is an intelligent Earth observation and environmental trend detection platform developed by Team Alpha StellarZ for NASA Space Apps Challenge 2026. It integrates NASA and partner datasets, including NASA POWER, MODIS, GISTEMP, GPM IMERG, EONET and FIRMS, to explore environmental changes across different geographical regions.

The platform provides 12 interactive modules, enabling users to explore satellite imagery, analyse 10 environmental variables, compare regional trends, detect opposite environmental patterns, monitor near-real-time events, and track space objects. It uses statistical methods such as the Mann-Kendall test and Sen's slope estimator to identify increasing or decreasing trends, measure rates of change, and evaluate statistical significance. An AI Science Assistant helps users understand scientific findings through accessible explanations.

EarthScope AI addresses NASA's challenge by transforming complex Earth science datasets into understandable visualizations and meaningful statistical insights. It is important because understanding environmental changes across regions helps improve climate awareness, support scientific education, and encourage data-driven investigation of Earth's interconnected systems.
details:
EarthScope AI – Project Details

Team: Alpha StellarZ
Challenge: Be an Earth System Trend Detective!

1. What does the project do, and how does it work?

EarthScope AI is an interactive, AI-assisted Earth observation and environmental trend analysis platform developed to help people understand how Earth's interconnected environmental systems are changing over time.

The platform collects and analyses data from NASA and partner sources, including NASA POWER, MODIS, GISTEMP, GPM IMERG and EONET. It enables users to explore satellite imagery, investigate ten environmental variables, analyse long-term trends, compare geographical regions, detect opposite environmental trends and monitor near-real-time environmental events.

EarthScope AI uses statistical techniques such as the Mann-Kendall test and Sen's slope estimator to identify increasing or decreasing trends, measure the rate of change and evaluate statistical significance. Its integrated AI Science Assistant helps users understand complex datasets, charts and scientific results through simple explanations. Users can also generate downloadable PDF, CSV and Excel reports for further research and analysis.

2. What benefits does it have?

EarthScope AI transforms complex environmental and satellite data into accessible information through interactive visualisations, statistical analysis and AI assistance.

Its key benefits include:

  • Helps students, researchers and the public explore environmental changes using NASA and partner datasets.
  • Enables users to compare long-term environmental trends across different geographical regions.
  • Identifies statistically significant increases and decreases in environmental variables.
  • Provides interactive satellite imagery and near-real-time environmental monitoring.
  • Uses AI assistance to explain scientific findings in an understandable way.
  • Supports education and research through downloadable reports and data exports.
  • Brings multiple Earth observation and analysis capabilities together in one platform.

3. What is the intended impact of the project?

Our primary goal is to make Earth science more accessible and encourage people to investigate the interconnected systems of our planet using real environmental data.

We aim to support environmental awareness, scientific education and data-driven research. By helping users identify, analyse and compare environmental trends across different regions, EarthScope AI encourages people to explore environmental changes, ask meaningful scientific questions and develop a deeper understanding of Earth's changing systems.

Ultimately, we hope the platform will serve as an educational and research-support tool that makes Earth observation data easier to explore and interpret.

4. What tools, coding languages, hardware or software did you use?

EarthScope AI was developed primarily using Python, with Streamlit as the main framework for building the interactive web application.

Our development tools and technologies include:

  • Python: Main programming language used for application development and data processing.
  • Streamlit: Used to build the interactive user interface, integrate application features and test functionality.
  • Pandas and NumPy: Used for data processing, calculations and numerical analysis.
  • Plotly: Used to create interactive charts, graphs and data visualisations.
  • SQLite: Used for local database storage.
  • Claude, Fable and Opus: AI-assisted development tools used to support coding, problem-solving, design and AI-related development.
  • NASA and partner data services: Used to access environmental, climate, satellite and natural-event datasets.
  • Render: Used to deploy and host the application online, making it accessible through a live web link.

The project is entirely software-based and does not require dedicated physical hardware. We tested and refined the application through Streamlit before deploying it using Render.

5. How is your project creative and innovative?

EarthScope AI brings multiple Earth science capabilities together in one interactive platform rather than limiting users to viewing individual datasets or charts.

Its innovative approach combines NASA-related data sources, statistical trend detection, regional comparisons, satellite imagery, near-real-time environmental monitoring, space-object tracking and AI-assisted scientific explanations.

One of its distinctive features is the Opposite Trend Detector, which helps users investigate whether two geographical regions are experiencing statistically significant environmental trends in opposite directions.

The AI Science Assistant further improves accessibility by helping users interpret their analysis results and understand scientific concepts. This combination of data science, Earth observation, statistical methods and AI creates a more interactive and approachable way to investigate our planet.

6. What factors did your team consider?

Throughout development, our team considered data reliability, scientific accuracy, accessibility, usability, performance and the limitations of environmental datasets.

We prioritised NASA and partner data sources to ensure that analyses are based on actual available observations and datasets rather than assumed values. We also considered API availability, missing credentials, connection failures and data accessibility.

To improve transparency, the application identifies features that require unavailable API keys or connections through clear DEMO MODE indicators. We incorporated statistical significance testing to help users distinguish statistically meaningful trends from results that may not be reliable.

Our team also considered the limitations of satellite observations and model-based datasets, the importance of clear visualisations and the need to make scientific information understandable to users with different levels of technical knowledge.

7. Team Contributions

EarthScope AI was developed through the collaborative efforts of Team Alpha StellarZ, with each member contributing their skills and expertise to bring the project to life.

  • Mr. Ameer Abdul Rahman – Team Leader and Project Lead: Led the entire project direction, vision, planning and development strategy. He guided the team throughout the project and, together with Abdul Gafar, was directly involved in coding, developing and integrating the platform.
  • Abdul Gafar – Co-Developer: Worked closely with Ameer on coding and developing the application, including its functionality, user interface and technical implementation.
  • Akhila, Zaki and Zahra – Data Research and Collection: Collaborated on collecting environmental data, researching NASA resources, identifying relevant datasets and gathering supporting information for the platform.
  • Mr. Dickens – AI, Design and Testing Support: Assisted with AI-related development, contributed to the design process and helped with testing the platform to improve its functionality and overall user experience.

The overall project vision, direction and leadership were led by Ameer, while the technical coding and development were carried out jointly by Ameer and Abdul Gafar. The research, data collection, AI assistance, design and testing contributions from the other team members helped transform the concept into a working online platform.

8. Live Project

EarthScope AI – Explore the platform:

https://earthscope-ai-7mti.onrender.com

EarthScope AI is an independent research prototype developed by Team Alpha StellarZ for NASA Space Apps Challenge 2026. It is not an official NASA product.
